title: Anthropic adds automated security review to Claude Code
summary: Anthropic introduced automated security reviews in Claude Code: a /security-review terminal command that scans a project for SQL injection, cross-site scripting, authentication and authorization flaws, insecure data handling and dependency vulnerabilities, explains each finding and can implement fixes, and a GitHub Action that reviews every new pull request, applies customizable rules to filter false positives, and posts inline comments with fix recommendations. Anthropic says its own internal use caught a remote code execution flaw exploitable through DNS rebinding in an internal tool and a server-side request forgery vulnerability in a credential proxy, both fixed before merge.
verification_note: URL fetched on 2026-10-17; the page is dated August 6, 2025 and published by Anthropic on claude.com. The /security-review command, the GitHub Action with inline PR comments, the listed vulnerability classes, and the DNS-rebinding RCE and SSRF examples caught before merge are all stated on the page. The page gives no quantitative metrics.
